event_description: 'Principal Only Payment' of -$2,900.00 which INCREASES the principal balance from $146,658.38 to $149,558.38
notes: What the row shows: a balance increase of $2,900.00 coded as a principal payment. No matching prior credit of $2,900.00 appears, so this is not a reversal of anything in the ledger. On a HELOC an additional draw would increase principal, which is the leading innocent explanation - but the ledger does not label draws, so the cause is [UNRESOLVED]. See CON-003.

event_description: Regular Payment of $2,028.22 posted (Flag 7)
The 12/01/22 Regular Payment is REVERSED (Rev Code 7), -$2,028.22
notes: Re-posted 12/15/22, so the net effect on this payment is neutral. The pattern of post-reverse-repost recurs in March 2023.

event_description: 'Principal Only Payment' of -$1,700.00 which increases the principal balance to $149,613.37
notes: Same pattern as EV-005: a balance increase coded as a principal payment, with no matching prior credit. [UNRESOLVED] as to cause.

event_description: The February and March 2023 Regular Payments, both posted 03/14/23, are REVERSED (Rev Code 7) on 03/23/23, and a late charge of $103.39 is re-assessed
notes: What the rows show: two payments applied on 03/14 and reversed nine days later, with the late charge that had been waived on 03/14 re-assessed on 03/23. The ledger gives no reason.

event_description: A single Unapplied Payment of $19,588.88 is received and held in suspense
notes: The largest single credit in the ledger. It is booked to suspense, not applied, and is then distributed across due dates 02/2023 through 10/2023 by a series of entries all dated 09/14/23.

event_description: Approximately eighteen offsetting Regular Payment / Unapplied Payment entries are booked on a single day, distributing the 09/13/23 suspense balance across due dates 02/01/23 through 10/01/23
notes: Confidence medium rather than high: the printed columns on several of these rows omit fields, and the running balance is difficult to reconcile line by line from the print-out alone. The overall effect - suspense distributed across back-dated periods - is clear; the per-row arithmetic is not independently verified.

event_description: Principal Only Payment of $10,000.00 reduces principal from $142,095.76 to $132,095.76
The 09/15/23 $10,000.00 principal payment is reversed, restoring principal to $142,095.76
notes: This negative entry IS a reversal - it has a matching prior credit eleven days earlier. Contrast EV-005 and EV-008, which do not.

event_description: Last payment activity of any kind in the ledger: two Regular Payments and a Principal Only Payment booked, leaving principal at $140,288.02
notes: After this date the principal balance never changes again through the 03/10/26 print date.
